ex.en: Our team communicates well.
I don't communicate well with my parents.
These days I communicate with friends by text.
The sandcastle my kid built fell down.
All our plans fell apart because of the rain.
I was crushed when I heard that.

I'm spending more than I earn.

fix.note: 르-irregular: 머물러요. Short form 머물다 only before consonants: 머물고, 머물 거예요.

ex.en: I'm staying in Seoul for a week.
Which hotel are you staying at?

ex.s: 지호 씨는 이모 집에 며칠 머물렀어요.
ex.en: Jiho stayed at his aunt's place for a few days.
Smoking is banned in this park.
Mom banned video games at night.

ex.s: 우리 회사는 회의 중에 휴대폰 사용을 금지해요.
ex.en: Our company bans phone use during meetings.

fix.note: 집안일 = housework. 'Inside the house' is spaced: 집 안.

ex.en: Everyone in my family is tall.
He comes from a good family.
On holidays we pay our respects to the family elders.

fix.note: 미소를 짓다 = to smile. Everyday speech often uses 웃음/웃다.

ex.en: The baby's smile is really cute.
Kevin always has a smile on his face.
That employee had a really bright smile.
Do you offer same-day delivery?
If you cancel on the day, there's no refund.
How about a day trip to Jeju?
This restaurant is relatively cheap.
It's relatively warm today.
This exam was fairly easy.
How did the salary negotiation go?
Negotiating the house price isn't easy.

ex.s: 지금 아이하고 게임 시간 협상 중이에요.
ex.en: I'm negotiating gaming time with my kid right now.
I'm going to see a play this weekend.
My daughter is in the school play.
I was in the drama club in college.

notes: 집안 wrongly glossed 'inside the house' (that is 집 안); 비교적 is an adverb; spacing 잘되다; unnatural collocations (수입이라서, 미소가 친절, 휴대폰을 금지); 머무르다 note now covers 머물다.
